To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) gene expression levels for most immune response genes analyzed are approximately normally distributed in healthy subjects; ( 2 ) the dynamic range of most genes is limited in healthy subjects, and (3) the expression of most genes in healthy subjects can be readily distinguished by gene expression analysis from that observed in subjects exposed to bacterial endotoxin.

(1) most immune response genes are expressed at approximately constant levels among healthy individuals; (2) most immune response gene expression levels are approximately log-nor- mally distributed among healthy individuals; and (3), following an injection of LPS, most immune response genes show a 10- to100-fold change in expression within 2 to5 h and a return to baseline within 21 h.

(1) gene expression levels for most immune response genes are approximately log-normal in healthy blood donors, (2) the dynamic range for expression of most immune response genes is small among healthy blood donors, and (3) the dynamic range is larger for immune response genes among healthy blood donors after an infusion of bacterial LPS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel technologies and assays to measure the expression of specific genes and gene products.
understanding the normal variations in gene expression in healthy subjects.
understanding how gene expression changes in response to infection, inflammation, and other disease states, and the use of these changes to diagnose, predict, and monitor disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the expression levels of the majority of immune response genes measured in whole blood from healthy individuals are approximately log-normal and have limited dynamic range of variation among individuals.

the dynamic range of gene expression of most immune response genes is quite limited in the healthy population and that a single blood sample from an individual is sufficient to define a normal expression range for that individual.

the expression of many genes in whole blood is relatively invariant across healthy individuals and that the expression of these genes can be readily distinguished when the individuals are exposed to a bacterial endotoxin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamic range of immune response genes is quite limited among healthy individuals, but that the dynamic range is quite large following exposure to an inflammatory stimulus.
the dynamic range of immune response gene expression is limited among healthy individuals, but that this range is expanded in the presence of disease or exposure to an inflammatory stimulus.
the expression of most immune response genes is relatively constant across individuals and that a small number of genes can be used to discriminate between normal and pathophysiological states.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamic range of gene expression is quite limited in normal subjects, and that this can be exploited to establish reference ranges for gene expression.

the dynamic range of immune response gene expression in healthy individuals is limited and can be readily distinguished, at the level of individual genes, from that seen in response to an immune challenge.
the dynamic range of gene expression is limited among healthy people and that the expression of many immune genes is approximately log-normaly distributed.
